pcs-6466: Two bits decide how the other sixty-four are read. Nothing else in the block is self-describing.
pcs-6466-struct: Header 01 means every octet is data, passed through untouched. The header itself carries no protection.
pcs-257: Seven bits saved per four blocks. Overhead falls from 3.125 to 0.39 percent, and the difference is what pays for parity.
pcs-257-lead: The common case costs exactly one bit, which is why the encoding is shaped this way round.
pcs-scramble: The receiver recovers its clock from transitions. The left trace starves it and drags the decision thresholds with it.
pcs-scramble-mult: The errored bit re-enters the shift register. Some of the burstiness FEC must handle is manufactured inside the PHY.
pcs-am-parts: You cannot identify a lane with a pattern that is identical everywhere, nor hunt a boundary with one that differs per lane.
pcs-dist-div: Because the logical count divides evenly, the same PCS drives four-lane and eight-lane interfaces with no change above the PMA.
pcs-lock-debug: Isolation to a single lane points at that lane's own path. A fault in configuration would take every lane down together.
fec-cw: 514 message symbols then 30 parity. Each cell here stands for sixteen real symbols.
fec-cw-budget: Identical bit damage, opposite outcome. This is the whole reason distribution and multiplexing are argued about.
fec-interleave: Two codewords interleaved ten bits at a time. Spreading means no single lane destroys a codeword alone; concentrating means a burst costs fewer symbols.
fec-il-sym: The same channel burst, mapped two ways. At 200G per lane the bursts are long enough that containment wins.
fec-dec-cliff: Flat, then vertical. A link reporting no loss may be sitting just left of the edge, and nothing downstream will say so.
fec-cc-inner: The inner code covers the segment with the worst statistics. The outer code still spans the whole path.
mac-frame: Widths in octets, drawn at the 64-octet minimum. The FCS covers everything from the destination address onward.
mac-rate: 84 octets on the wire carry 46 octets of payload. This includes the preamble, frame, and required inter-frame gap; the same 26 octets of overhead barely register against a 1500-octet payload.
pma-pam4: Four levels share the amplitude range NRZ used for two, so each eye is about a third the height. That is the roughly 9.5 dB penalty, drawn.
pma-eq: One wrong decision feeds the next. With a one-tap DFE at coefficient 1 the chance of continuing is about 3/4 per symbol.
aui-c2m: Two vendors, one channel. The specification divides the budget at the connector and defines compliance points either side, so neither has to test against the other.
pmd-tdecq: Two vertical histograms at 0.45 and 0.55 unit intervals, spanning all four levels. The noise they capture is compared with an ideal receiver, and the difference in dB is the penalty.
rs-fault: The far end's transmitter is the broken part, but it sees good data coming back. Remote fault is how it finds out.
form-lanes: The cage decides how many electrical lanes arrive; the PMD decides how many optical lanes leave. They need not match.
macsec-frame: Widths in octets, drawn with a 16-octet SecTAG and a 16-octet ICV - the usual case, and 32 octets of addition.
fec-cc-seg: Segmenting contains errors per hop but re-encodes an uncorrected error as apparently clean data for the next hop.
